<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Jordan runs a second Claude Code setup through a shell function (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.claude-alt" claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`). pij can adopt such a seat but cannot spawn one, and revive relaunches it as plain `claude` in the default home, where `--resume` misses its transcript. This plan adds named alternate launches per harness in one TOML file, a `--alt` spawn flag, the alt recorded on the seat and reused by revive, and the Claude binder reading the alt's home.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Any harness can be started an alternate way by name, configured once in pij.
- A seat started with an alt is revived with the same alt, or refused loudly, never relaunched with the default.
- A Claude alt seat binds and resumes in its own home.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- No per-alt model, effort or role defaults: those stay spawn flags.
- No `--alt` on revive to change a seat's alt.
- No removal of the existing `~/.claude-alt` probe in `claude_homes_from` (proposed to the prime separately).
- No hook install into a home configured after the daemon started: that happens at the next daemon start, and doctor says so.
- No `pij-rs doctor harness-alts` verb (scope cut by the prime, 2026-11-22).

| ac-0001 | `&lt;state-dir&gt;/harness-alts.toml` (`~/.pij-rs/harness-alts.toml`) holds one table per alternate launch, `[&lt;harness&gt;.&lt;name&gt;]`, with optional `env` (a string table), `bin` (an absolute executable) and `args` (strings appended to the launch). A leading `~` in an env value or `bin` is the user's home. A missing file means no alts. The file is refused whole, naming the file and the fault, for an unknown harness key or field, an alt name outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,32}`, an env key outside `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` or starting `PIJ_`, a control character in any value, a relative `bin`, or a relative Claude `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. | ac-0002 | `pij-rs spawn --harness &lt;h&gt; --alt &lt;name&gt;` launches with the alt's env (applied after `PIJ_SESSION_ID`/`PIJ_SPAWN_ID` and before pij's own harness env, so pij's own values win), its `bin` in place of the harness name, and its `args` after pij's own. <a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

Code map (main 3707709e). Spawn argv: `pij_harnesses::build_spawn_plan` (crates/harnesses/src/spawn.rs) builds `env PIJ_SESSION_ID=.. PIJ_SPAWN_ID=.. [COPILOT_*] <harness> <args>`; `--bin` replaces the harness name after `validate_executable_override`. The daemon's `launch_owned` (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs) builds the plan and writes the descriptor; revive (crates/daemon/src/http/revive.rs) rebuilds a `SpawnRequest` from the prior row (`executable: None`, so `--bin` is not durable today). Durable per-seat launch facts precedent: `cache_proxy` (JSON TEXT column, migration 0047; `opted_out` survives revive). Registration clones the existing row, so a new descriptor field survives binding unless cleared. Claude binder (crates/daemon/src/claude_bind.rs `matching_record`) reads only `$HOME/.claude/sessions`. `claude_homes_from` already appends `~/.claude-alt` when it exists. Config precedent: `cache-proxy.toml` in the state dir, parsed with `toml` + `deny_unknown_fields`. The roster table is rendered by both `crates/cli/src/roster.rs` and `.omp/extensions/pij/core/roster-table.ts`, pinned by golden `list-sized`.

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An alt's env carries a secret (an API key) that then shows in a receipt or doctor. | Medium | Medium | Only the alt name and the Claude home are recorded on the seat; doctor prints env keys, never values. The launch argv carries the env as `env` does today for pij's own variables (visible to `ps`), stated in the docs. |
| An alt home configured after the daemon started lacks pij's hooks. | Medium | Low | The binder needs no hook (it reads Claude's own session record). `just doctor`'s claude-hooks rows list the home with its fix; docs say hooks land at the next daemon start. |
| An edit moves an alt's Claude home, and revive then resumes in a home without the transcript. | Low | Medium | The brief asks that edits apply. Docs say so; the recorded home shows in `pij-rs state` so the change is visible. |

## Execution Guardrails
